note: All three groups were applied on 2026-11-22 by Garo's ruling. Each find string occurred exactly once in the named field at the baseline.

corrections.find: translates every Aramaic phrase
corrections.replace: translates most of the Aramaic phrases
corrections.basis: Tagged Greek: Rabbi (9:5, 11:21, 14:45), Rabbouni (10:51) and Hosanna (11:9-10) are left untranslated.

corrections.find: John in the desert, quoting Isaiah, pointing past himself
corrections.replace: A line from the prophets, then John in the desert, pointing past himself
corrections.basis: Hosted 1:2: "As it is written in the prophets". The narrator quotes; John does not.

corrections.find: To turn around and go a different way. It can carry regret, but the core of the word is change of direction, not feeling bad.
corrections.replace: To change your mind, and so your course. It can carry regret, but the base sense of the Greek word is a change of mind.
corrections.basis: Thayer's, metanoeo: "to change one's mind, i. e. to repent". Strong's: "to think differently or afterwards". Neither gives "turn".

corrections.find: Five short confrontations, back to back.
corrections.replace: Four short confrontations, back to back.
corrections.basis: Hosted chapter 2 has four (2:6-7, 2:16, 2:18, 2:24). The fifth in the run is 3:1-6.

corrections.find: It marks intense devotion to the law and, in this period, sympathy with armed resistance to Rome — which makes the presence of a tax collector in the same group of twelve remarkable.
corrections.replace: It marks intense devotion to the law. A generation later it was the name of a party in the armed revolt against Rome. Either way, the presence of a tax collector in the same group of twelve is remarkable.
corrections.basis: Josephus, War 4.3.9: the party name appears during the revolt of AD 66-70 ("that was the name they went by"). No source read shows the armed sense about AD 30.

corrections.find: The Greek phrase covers his relatives or close associates
corrections.replace: The translation here says 'his friends'; the Greek phrase covers his relatives or close associates
corrections.basis: Hosted 3:21 reads "his friends", while the question says "his family". Thayer's on the Greek phrase: "his kinsmen, relations".

corrections.find: he stops it with two words
corrections.replace: he stops it with two short commands
corrections.basis: Hosted 4:39: "Peace! Be still!" (three English words). The tagged Greek has two words.

corrections.find: Is 'smaller than all the seeds on earth' just wrong?
corrections.replace: Is 'less than all the seeds that are on the earth' just wrong?
corrections.basis: Hosted 4:31: "less than all the seeds that are on the earth".

corrections.find: A corpse, a chronic discharge of blood, and a graveyard were the three great sources of ritual defilement in Jewish law.
corrections.replace: A corpse, a chronic discharge of blood, and a grave each made a person ritually unclean in Jewish law (Numbers 5:2; 19:16; Leviticus 15:25).
corrections.basis: Hosted Numbers 5:2 names the leper, the discharge and the corpse; Mishnah Kelim 1:1-4 lists more. Nothing read ranks these three as "the three great sources".

corrections.find: Most read it the way Jesus uses the word elsewhere — death described as sleep
corrections.replace: Most read it the way Jesus speaks of Lazarus in John 11:11-14 — death described as sleep
corrections.basis: Tagged Greek: the verb in 5:39 is used elsewhere in Mark only for ordinary sleep (4:27, 4:38, 13:36, 14:37-41). The parallel is hosted John 11:11-14.

corrections.find: Mark uses 'hardened' for the opposition in 3:5 — using the same word for the Twelve is deliberate and unflattering.
corrections.replace: Mark speaks of the 'hardening' of the opposition's hearts in 3:5 — using the same root for the Twelve is deliberate and unflattering.
corrections.basis: Tagged Greek: 3:5 has the noun porosis; 6:52 and 8:17 have the verb poroo. Same root, not the same word.

corrections.find: The Greek word covers a builder working in wood and stone — a general craftsman rather than specifically a furniture maker.
corrections.replace: The Greek word means a worker in wood, and more loosely a builder or craftsman — not specifically a furniture maker.
corrections.basis: Thayer's, tekton: "a worker in wood, a carpenter". Wiktionary: "one who works with wood: carpenter, builder"; "any craftsman". No lexicon read gives stone.

corrections.find: Aramaic for 'dedicated to God.'
corrections.replace: Hebrew for an offering, 'given to God.'
corrections.basis: Thayer's, korban: "Hebrew ... an offering". The Hebrew word is in hosted Leviticus 1:2. Hosted Mark 7:11: "given to God".

corrections.find: Originally a Greek stage term for an actor.
corrections.replace: In ordinary Greek, a word for a stage actor.
corrections.basis: Thayer's, hypokrites: "1. one who answers, an interpreter. 2. an actor, stage-player". The stage sense is not listed as the first.

corrections.find: Galilee had seen it used.
corrections.replace: The country had seen it used: a generation earlier a Roman governor crucified about two thousand rebels (Josephus, Antiquities 17.10.10).
corrections.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 17.10.10 and War 2.5.2: about two thousand crucified, sought "into the country"; no region is named. In Galilee, Sepphoris was burned and its people enslaved (17.10.9); crucifixion is not mentioned there.

corrections.find: within a day the group is arguing about rank
corrections.replace: before the chapter ends the group is arguing about rank
corrections.basis: Hosted 9:30 and 9:33: they travel through Galilee to Capernaum first. No time is given.

corrections.find: Mark keeps the Aramaic term.
corrections.replace: Mark keeps the Hebrew word.
corrections.basis: Thayer's, rabbi: "Hebrew ... properly, my great one". Strong's: "of Hebrew origin".

corrections.find: the underlying picture is a cursed valley, permanent burning, and rubbish that is never dealt with.
corrections.replace: the underlying picture is a cursed valley and permanent burning.
corrections.basis: The burning rubbish heap is first attributed to Rabbi David Kimhi, about AD 1200; "there is no direct archaeological nor literary evidence for it" (Wikipedia, "Gehenna"). Thayer's (1889) repeats the tradition.

corrections.find: the only person in the gospels who declines a direct invitation
corrections.replace: the one person in Mark who walks away from a direct invitation
corrections.basis: Hosted Luke 9:59: "Follow me!" ... "Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father."

corrections.find: he calls Jesus 'son of David,' a messianic title, and nobody silences him.
corrections.replace: he calls Jesus 'son of David,' a messianic title; the crowd tries to quiet him, and Jesus does not.
corrections.basis: Hosted 10:48: "Many rebuked him, that he should be quiet".

corrections.find: Bartimaeus shouts it in public and is not corrected
corrections.replace: Bartimaeus shouts it in public and Jesus does not silence him
corrections.basis: Hosted 10:48-49: the crowd rebukes him; Jesus calls him over.

corrections.find: A Roman general entered a city on a warhorse.
corrections.replace: A conqueror came on a warhorse or in a chariot.
corrections.basis: No source was read for the Roman general. Hosted Zechariah 9:10, already cited in the answer, names the chariot and the horse.

corrections.find: standing in the temple, run without stopping to pack
corrections.replace: standing where it ought not, run without stopping to pack
corrections.basis: Hosted 13:14: "standing where it ought not". "In the holy place" is Matthew 24:15.

corrections.find: set up a pagan altar in the Jerusalem temple and sacrificed a pig on it — an act remembered with horror and recounted in 1 Maccabees.
corrections.replace: set up a pagan altar in the Jerusalem temple (1 Maccabees 1:54-59) and, Josephus says, sacrificed swine on it — an act remembered with horror.
corrections.basis: Hosted 1 Maccabees 1:54 and 1:59 tell of the altar; 1:47 has the order to sacrifice swine. The swine on the temple altar is Josephus, Antiquities 12.5.4.

corrections.find: Trial — outer half
corrections.replace: Trial — inner story
corrections.basis: Hosted 14:54 and 14:66-72: Peter's story opens before the trial and closes after it, so the trial is the inner part.

corrections.find: Denial — inner half resolved
corrections.replace: Denial — outer story resolved
corrections.basis: Same: Peter's denial is the frame around the trial.

corrections.find: his one question is whether Jesus claims to be King of the Jews
corrections.replace: his question is whether Jesus claims to be King of the Jews
corrections.basis: Hosted 15:2 and 15:4: Pilate asks Jesus a second question ("Have you no answer?").

corrections.find: Mark uses the Latin term, as he does 'cohort' — a unit of several hundred soldiers.
corrections.replace: Mark uses the Latin term, as he does for 'centurion' in verse 39. The cohort called together here was a unit of several hundred soldiers.
corrections.basis: Tagged Greek: praitorion (15:16) and kenturion (15:39) are Latin loanwords (Thayer's: "a Latin word"). For speira, "cohort", the lexicons differ: Thayer's treats it as Greek, Strong's as Latin in origin.

corrections.find: Crucified bodies were normally left to hang or thrown into a common grave; that was part of the punishment.
corrections.replace: Under Roman practice crucified bodies were often left to hang; Jewish custom was to bury them before sunset (Deuteronomy 21:22-23; Josephus, War 4.5.2).
corrections.basis: Josephus, War 4.5.2: the Jews "took down those that were condemned and crucified, and buried them before the going down of the sun". Hosted Deuteronomy 21:22-23. The Roman practice rests on a secondary summary only; no source read mentions a common grave.

corrections.find: So do the oldest Syriac, an old Latin manuscript, and the earliest Armenian and Georgian versions.
corrections.replace: Verses 9-20 are also missing from the oldest Syriac copy, from one old Latin manuscript (which has a short ending instead), and from many Armenian and some Georgian manuscripts.
corrections.basis: Codex Bobiensis is "the only known example of the shorter ending added directly to Mark 16:8" (Wikipedia, "Codex Bobiensis", citing Aland and Metzger), so it does not stop at verse 8. Wikipedia, "Mark 16": "many Armenian manuscripts, some Georgian manuscripts".

softer.find: Second, the Aramaic behind 'that' can carry the sense of result rather than purpose
softer.replace: Second, some scholars argue that an Aramaic word behind 'that' could mean result rather than purpose
softer.basis: A proposal about an Aramaic saying behind the Greek, tied to T. W. Manson and an ambiguous particle in the Targum of Isaiah 6:9. It is disputed. Secondary summaries only.

softer.find: A good harvest in that agriculture returned something in the range of tenfold.
softer.replace: On one common estimate, a good harvest in that agriculture returned something in the range of tenfold.
softer.basis: Dalman's estimate (tenfold good, about sevenfold average) as reported in R. K. McIver, New Testament Studies 40 (1994), who disputes that thirtyfold was out of the ordinary. Abstract and excerpt only.

softer.find: Notice he is not Jewish — the silence rule does not apply out here.
softer.replace: Notice where he is — the Decapolis, Gentile country — and the silence rule does not apply out here.
softer.basis: Hosted 5:20 names the region. The chapter does not say what people the man belongs to.

softer.find: is the same construction used for the divine name in Exodus 3:14
softer.replace: is the same two Greek words that open the divine name in the Greek version of Exodus 3:14 — though they are also the ordinary way to say 'it's me'
softer.basis: Tagged Greek 6:50: ego eimi. Septuagint Exodus 3:14: Ego eimi ho on. The same two words are everyday Greek, so the echo is a reading.

softer.find: Mark divides the night into four Roman watches rather than the three used in Jewish reckoning — a small sign of who he was writing for.
softer.replace: Mark divides the night into four watches, the Roman way; older Israelite reckoning had three (Judges 7:19).
softer.basis: Thayer's, phylake: before the exile the Israelites had three watches; later "they adopted the Roman custom of dividing the night into four watches". So four watches do not mark out a non-Jewish reader.

softer.find: Mark uses the Roman 'fourth watch of the night' rather than a Jewish time reckoning
softer.replace: Mark counts the night in four watches, the Roman way

softer.find: The only time in the gospels anyone wins an exchange with Jesus
softer.replace: The one time in Mark that anyone wins an exchange with Jesus
softer.basis: A claim about all four gospels that was not checked. Narrowed to the book the guide covers.

softer.find: this is the one conversation in the gospels that Jesus concedes
softer.replace: this is the one conversation in Mark that Jesus concedes

softer.find: By this period the title carried a widespread expectation of national deliverance from Rome
softer.replace: By this period many attached to the title an expectation of national deliverance from Rome
softer.basis: The Mark briefing: Jewish hopes "take several forms — political, national, and religious — rather than one single expectation".

softer.find: In that society a child had no legal standing, no status
softer.replace: In that society a child had no standing of its own, no status
softer.basis: ISBE, "Child": "Children were subject to the father". Hosted Galatians 4:1. Nothing read says a child had no legal standing.

softer.find: Collection receptacles in the temple's Court of the Women, where
softer.replace: Collection chests in the temple, by tradition in the Court of the Women, where
softer.basis: Mishnah Shekalim 6:5: "thirteen collection horns in the Temple". It names no court.

softer.find: Passion narrative, the oldest continuous block of gospel tradition, with
softer.replace: Passion narrative, often thought to be the oldest continuous block of gospel tradition, with
softer.basis: A source-critical proposal. No source was read for it.

softer.find: Because carrying water was women's work, so a man doing it stood out in a crowded festival city.
softer.replace: Because drawing water was usually women's work (Genesis 24:11), so a man carrying a jar would stand out in a crowded festival city.
softer.basis: Hosted Genesis 24:11: "the time that women go out to draw water". No reference work read says a man with a jar would stand out.

softer.find: while the Galilean pilgrims who lined the road are elsewhere
softer.replace: and nothing says the pilgrims who lined the road are there
softer.basis: The chapter does not say where they were.

softer.find: the thorn crown parodies the radiate crowns on imperial coins
softer.replace: the thorn crown may parody the radiate crowns shown on coins
softer.basis: A proposal by H. St. J. Hart, Journal of Theological Studies 3 (1952). Secondary summaries only.

softer.find: A heavy woven veil separating the innermost sanctuary
softer.replace: Usually taken as the inner veil: a heavy woven curtain separating the innermost sanctuary
softer.basis: Josephus, War 5.5.4-5 describes two veils. Mark does not say which. Hosted Hebrews 9:3 calls the inner one "the second veil".

softer.find: and Mark, the earliest, has no male witness
softer.replace: and Mark, which most scholars date earliest, has no male witness
softer.basis: The Mark briefing: Markan priority is "the majority position"; Matthew first is "still defended today".

softer.find: added by a hand other than the one that wrote the rest
softer.replace: which most modern editions mark as a later addition
softer.basis: The Mark briefing lists both positions on the ending; its settled line is that modern editions flag the longer ending.

claims.claim: 'immediately' twelve times in this chapter
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: euthys 12 times in chapter 1. Hosted English: "immediately" 12 times.

claims.claim: in ordinary Greek, an announcement of a victory or a ruler's arrival
claims.basis: Priene calendar inscription, 9 BC: the birthday of Augustus as "the beginning of the good tidings" (Wikipedia, "Priene calendar inscription"). Thayer's and Wiktionary: "a reward for good news", "good news". No page read gives "news of a victory"; the classical lexicon would not load.

claims.claim: means 'anointed one'; the Hebrew equivalent is Messiah
claims.basis: Hosted John 1:41: "the Messiah! (which is, being interpreted, Christ)".

claims.claim: their authority came from citing tradition
claims.basis: Nothing read.

claims.claim: what the kingdom means; why Jesus orders silence
claims.basis: The briefing treats the silence orders as "an interpretation rather than a settled fact".

claims.claim: Capernaum, a fishing town on the Sea of Galilee
claims.basis: Hosted 1:16-21: fishermen at the lake, then Capernaum.

claims.claim: a capital charge under the law
claims.basis: Hosted Leviticus 24:16.

claims.claim: flat roofs of beams, branches and dried mud; used for sleeping and drying grain; reached from outside
claims.basis: Smith's Bible Dictionary, "House": "plaster of mud and straw laid upon boughs or rafters"; roofs used "as sleeping-places" and for "drying corn". Hosted Mark 13:15 and Joshua 2:6. Smith's puts the stairs in a corner of the court.

claims.claim: tax collectors in Galilee worked for Herod Antipas; they kept what they raised above the quota
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 17.11.4: Perea and Galilee paid their tribute to Antipas. Easton's, "Publican": "one who farmed the taxes". Hosted Luke 3:13. Keeping the excess is implied, not stated, in what was read.

claims.claim: one fast day was required; devout groups fasted regularly
claims.basis: Hosted Leviticus 16:29-31 and Luke 18:12.

claims.claim: some take the Greek as 'in the passage about Abiathar'
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: the same construction at 12:26, which the hosted text renders "about the Bush".

claims.claim: 'son of man' can mean 'a human being'; Daniel 7:13
claims.basis: Hosted Aramaic of Daniel 7:13 has the phrase. Everyday Aramaic usage was not checked.

claims.claim: claiming kingship got you executed in the province
claims.basis: Nothing read.

claims.claim: a principle for reading every rule in the book
Mark translates it as 'Sons of Thunder'
claims.basis: Hosted 3:17.

claims.claim: healing on the Sabbath was allowed only when a life was in danger
claims.basis: Mishnah Yoma 8:6: "a case of uncertainty concerning a life-threatening situation overrides Shabbat". The Mishnah was written down about AD 200.

claims.claim: the Pharisees had no love for Herod's court
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 17.2.4: above six thousand Pharisees refused the oath of loyalty. "A devout renewal movement" was not checked.

claims.claim: twelve is 'almost certainly' a claim to restart Israel
the Greek phrase covers relatives; the verb means to seize
claims.basis: Tagged Greek 3:21; the same verb is used for arrests at 6:17, 12:12, 14:1, 14:44, 14:46. Thayer's on the phrase: "his kinsmen".

claims.claim: what the unforgivable sin is
the brothers are unconvinced; James later leads the Jerusalem church
claims.basis: Hosted John 7:5 and Galatians 1:19.

claims.claim: the lake is about 13 miles by 7, about 700 feet below sea level, with sudden squalls
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Sea of Galilee": 21 km (13 mi) long, 13 km (8 mi) wide, 209-215 m below sea level. Smith's: "frequent sudden and violent storms". The page read gives 8 miles wide, not 7.

claims.claim: 'rebuked' is the verb used on the unclean spirit in 1:25
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: epitimao at 1:25 and 4:39; phimoo ("be silent") only at 1:25 and 4:39.

claims.claim: seed was scattered first and ploughed in afterward
claims.basis: Smith's, "Agriculture": "the seed being scattered broad cast and ploughed in afterwards". Mishnah Shabbat 7:2 lists sowing before ploughing. ISBE and hosted Isaiah 28:24 also show ploughing first, so both orders are attested.

claims.claim: a mustard seed was a proverbial figure for something tiny
claims.basis: Mishnah Niddah 5:2: "even like the size of a mustard seed".

claims.claim: 'they feared a great fear'
claims.basis: Tagged Greek 4:41.

claims.claim: mastery of the sea belongs to God (Psalm 107:29, Job 38:8-11)
claims.basis: Hosted Psalm 107:29.

claims.claim: 'Daughter' is the only time he calls anyone that
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: the only use as an address in Mark is 5:34. Outside Mark, hosted Luke 23:28 has "Daughters of Jerusalem".

claims.claim: a legion was several thousand men
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Roman legion": about 5,200.

claims.claim: the Decapolis: 'ten cities', Greek-speaking and largely Gentile
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Decapolis": "ten Greek Hellenistic cities". Josephus, War 3.9.7. Pliny would not load.

claims.claim: Leviticus 15 on a discharge of blood
claims.basis: Hosted Leviticus 15:25-27.

claims.claim: four Aramaic sayings kept, each with a translation
claims.basis: Tagged Greek and hosted text: 5:41, 7:34, 14:36, 15:34.

claims.claim: why the silence rule is reversed; kept words as eyewitness memory
claims.basis: The briefing leaves both open.

claims.claim: Antipas, son of Herod the Great, ruler of Galilee and Perea, not a king in Roman law
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 17.8.1: "tetrarch of Galilee and Perea". Hosted Luke 3:1 and Matthew 14:1.

claims.claim: Herod the Great died around 4 BC
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Herod the Great": 4 BC (Schürer) or 1 BC (Steinmann).

claims.claim: Catholic tradition reads 'brothers' as close kin
claims.basis: Jerome, Against Helvidius: only the editor's summary ("first cousins") was read word for word.

claims.claim: a denarius was a day's wage; two hundred is about eight months
claims.basis: Hosted Matthew 20:2.

claims.claim: the first feeding is on the Jewish side, the second on the Gentile side
claims.basis: An inference from hosted 7:31; widely held.

claims.claim: God 'passes by' Moses and Elijah (Exodus 33, 1 Kings 19)
claims.basis: Septuagint Exodus 33:19, 33:22 and 1 Kings 19:11 use the verb Mark has at 6:48. The hosted English has "pass by" in each.

claims.claim: from Numbers 27:17 and Ezekiel 34
claims.basis: Hosted Numbers 27:17 and Ezekiel 34:5.

claims.claim: Jesus goes home to Nazareth
claims.basis: Hosted 6:1 says "his own country"; 1:9 names Nazareth.

claims.claim: 'Greek' here means Gentile, not Greek by descent
claims.basis: Thayer's, Hellenis: "a Gentile woman; not a Jewess".

claims.claim: Aramaic for 'be opened'
claims.basis: Hosted 7:34; the briefing.

claims.claim: the law requires washing of priests; the practice extended priestly purity to daily life
claims.basis: Hosted Exodus 30:19-21 for the priests. The extension was not checked.

claims.claim: the word for 'dogs' is a diminutive
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: kynarion at 7:27-28; kyon does not occur in Mark. Thayer's: "a little dog". No lexicon read says house dog or street dog; the table is in 7:28.

claims.claim: the quotation of 7:8
claims.basis: A contiguous part of hosted 7:8, which the check allows.

claims.claim: the silence orders stop after the crucifixion
claims.basis: Hosted 9:9 sets the limit at the resurrection.

claims.claim: Caesarea Philippi: at the foot of Hermon, a shrine to Pan, built up by Philip and named for Caesar, about 25 miles north of the lake
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 18.2.1 and War 2.9.1 (Philip, Caesarea); Antiquities 15.10.3 and War 1.21.3 (the temple by Panium). Wikipedia, "Banias": foot of Mount Hermon, a shrine to Pan. The distance is not on a page read; the two sets of coordinates are about 25 miles apart.

claims.place: glossary: Take up your cross, question 9
claims.claim: the condemned carried the cross; a Roman execution for rebels and slaves
claims.basis: Hosted John 19:17 and Mark 15:21 for the carrying. Josephus, Antiquities 17.10.10 for rebels. Slaves: a secondary summary only.

claims.claim: the only two-stage healing; Mark alone records it
claims.basis: Among the four hosted gospels, "like trees" occurs only at Mark 8:24. "The only one in the gospels" was not otherwise checked.

claims.claim: the Greek word for 'life' also means soul or self
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: psyche at 8:35-37. Strong's: "soul, life, self".

claims.claim: what 'Christ' meant; why he orders silence
literally something like 'my great one'
claims.basis: Thayer's: "properly, my great one, my honorable sir".

claims.claim: the large kind turned by a donkey
claims.basis: Tagged Greek 9:42: mylos onikos. Thayer's: "turned by an ass".

claims.claim: Gehenna is the Valley of Hinnom, a site of child sacrifice
claims.basis: Hosted 2 Kings 23:10 and Jeremiah 7:31.

claims.claim: Moses and Elijah both met God on a mountain
claims.basis: Hosted Exodus 24 and 1 Kings 19.

claims.claim: an eighteen-mile climb from Jericho to Jerusalem
claims.basis: Josephus, War 4.8.3: "an hundred and fifty furlongs from Jerusalem", about 17 miles.

claims.claim: two schools disputed the grounds for divorce in Deuteronomy 24:1
claims.basis: Mishnah Gittin 9:10 (Shammai, Hillel, Akiva).

claims.claim: beyond the Jordan was Antipas's territory, where John was killed
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 17.8.1 (Perea) and 18.5.2 (Macherus).

claims.claim: the certificate showed a woman was free to remarry
claims.basis: Mishnah Gittin 9:3: "You are hereby permitted to marry any man." Her being destitute without it was not checked.

claims.claim: Jewish law gave only the husband the act of divorce; Roman law let a wife begin it
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 15.7.10: "not according to the Jewish laws; for with us it is lawful for a husband to do so". Mishnah Ketubot 7:10: a court may force the husband. Roman law was not checked.

claims.claim: the 'Needle's Eye gate' is medieval and has no evidence
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Eye of a needle": put forward since the 9th to 11th century; "no evidence for the existence of such a gate".

claims.claim: 'ransom' was the price to free a slave or a captive
claims.basis: Thayer's, lytron: "the price for redeeming, ransom (paid for slaves ... for captives".

claims.claim: an allotted portion of suffering; used again in 14:36
claims.basis: Hosted Isaiah 51:17 and Jeremiah 25:15; tagged Greek 10:38-39 and 14:36.

claims.claim: the cloak was a beggar's bedding
claims.basis: Hosted Exodus 22:26-27. Collecting coins on it was not checked.

claims.claim: Mark alone records that Jesus loved him
claims.basis: No such line in hosted Matthew 19:16-22 or Luke 18:18-23.

claims.claim: at Passover the city filled and Rome posted extra troops
claims.basis: Josephus, War 2.12.1: "a Roman cohort stood over the cloisters of the temple" at the feast, as "they always were armed, and kept guard at the festivals". Antiquities 20.5.3. Crowd numbers were not read word for word.

claims.claim: Hosanna is Hebrew for 'save now', from Psalm 118
claims.basis: Hosted Hebrew of Psalm 118:25. Thayer's: "save, I pray".

claims.claim: a fig tree in leaf normally carries small early figs
claims.basis: ISBE, "Fig": "every fig-tree which is going to bear fruit at all will have some taksh ('immature figs') upon it".

claims.claim: pilgrims needed temple currency; money-changers served them
claims.basis: Mishnah Shekalim 1:3: on the 25th of Adar "the money changers sat in the Temple".

claims.claim: the outer courts covered about thirty-five acres, with a Roman garrison overlooking
claims.basis: Josephus, War 5.5.8 (Antonia). The area (36 to 37 acres) comes from a helper's summary of Wikipedia, "Temple Mount", not from text read word for word.

claims.claim: moving a mountain was a figure of speech
claims.basis: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 64a: "one who uproots mountains", for a sharp scholar. Centuries later than Mark.

claims.claim: verse 26 is missing from the oldest manuscripts; it resembles Matthew 6:15
claims.basis: Wikipedia, list of verses not in modern translations: "not in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Regius"; "very similar to Matthew 6:15".

claims.claim: answering a question with a question was a recognised rabbinic style
claims.basis: Nothing read.

claims.claim: the Sadducees: priestly aristocracy, the written law above tradition, no resurrection
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 13.10.6 and 18.1.4; War 2.8.14.

claims.claim: they disappear after AD 70
claims.basis: Nothing read.

claims.claim: the coin: the emperor's portrait and a title claiming divine descent
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Tribute penny": "Ti[berivs] Caesar Divi Avg[vsti] F[ilivs] Avgvstvs". Hosted Matthew 20:2 for the day's wage.

claims.claim: named for its first Hebrew word; recited twice daily
claims.basis: Hosted Hebrew of Deuteronomy 6:4. Mishnah Berakhot 1:1-2 (evening and morning).

claims.claim: two lepta make a quadrans, a Roman coin
claims.basis: Tagged Greek 12:42. Thayer's: "a Latin word, quadrans".

claims.claim: a revolt had been raised over this tax
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 18.1.1 and War 2.8.1. Hosted Acts 5:37.

claims.claim: 'image' is the word of Genesis 1:27
claims.basis: Tagged Greek 12:16: eikon. Septuagint Genesis 1:27: kat' eikona theou.

claims.claim: the last thing he does in the temple
claims.basis: Hosted 13:1.

claims.claim: who the parable's figures are; what the riddle proves
Herod's temple: decades of building, huge stones, among the largest sanctuaries
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 15.11.1 and 15.11.3 (stones 25 cubits long) and 20.9.7 (finished much later). Hosted John 2:20. Wikipedia, "Western Stone": 250-300 tonnes.

claims.claim: AD 70: Titus took Jerusalem; Josephus was present
claims.basis: Josephus, War 6.4 and 7.1.1; Against Apion 1.9.

claims.claim: Antiochus IV set up a pagan altar in 167 BC
claims.basis: Hosted 1 Maccabees 1:54. The year is from Wikipedia.

claims.claim: a standard Jewish image for distress before God acts
claims.basis: Nothing read.

claims.claim: tradition says believers fled Jerusalem before the siege
claims.basis: Eusebius, Church History 3.5.3: to "a certain town of Perea called Pella".

claims.claim: the Greek for 'generation' can mean a kind or race
claims.basis: Thayer's, genea: "men of the same stock, a family"; "a perverse race".

claims.claim: the four times named are the four night watches
claims.basis: Hosted 13:35. Thayer's on the four Roman watches. Matching them to the next two chapters is a reading.

claims.claim: three hundred denarii is about a year's wages; nard came from the Himalayan region
claims.basis: Hosted Matthew 20:2. Wikipedia, "Spikenard": the plant "grows in the Himalayas". The sealed jar was not checked.

claims.claim: kings were anointed with oil on the head
claims.basis: Hosted 1 Samuel 10:1 and 2 Kings 9:6.

claims.claim: the cup as an image of judgment
claims.basis: Hosted Isaiah 51:17 and Jeremiah 25:15.

claims.claim: Abba: the Aramaic word for father, not baby talk; used in Romans 8:15 and Galatians 4:6
claims.basis: Thayer's: Aramaic, "father". Hosted Romans 8:15 and Galatians 4:6. "Not baby talk" follows J. Barr, Journal of Theological Studies 39 (1988), known here from summaries only.

claims.claim: the high priest tears his clothes, the prescribed response to blasphemy
claims.basis: Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:5: the judges "stand on their feet and make a tear in their garments".

claims.claim: 'I am' echoes Exodus 3:14
claims.basis: Tagged Greek 14:62 and Septuagint Exodus 3:14 share the two words. That it is an echo is a reading.

claims.claim: an invented scene would have been tidied
the quotation of 14:9
claims.basis: A contiguous part of hosted 14:9.

claims.claim: Golgotha was outside the city wall
claims.basis: Hosted Hebrews 13:12 and John 19:20.

claims.claim: the name means 'son of the father'
claims.basis: Thayer's: "son of a father".

claims.claim: for slaves, rebels and the lowest criminals; citizens normally exempt
claims.basis: A secondary summary only; Cicero would not load.

claims.claim: counted from sunrise
claims.basis: Hosted John 11:9: "twelve hours of daylight".

claims.claim: an officer over about eighty men
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Centurion": "a century was typically composed of around 80 men".

claims.claim: purple was the royal colour and very costly
claims.basis: ISBE and American Tract Society dictionary, "Purple": "the royal color"; "a very high price".

claims.claim: the Most Holy Place, entered by the high priest once a year
claims.basis: Hosted Hebrews 9:3 and 9:7.

claims.claim: Mark uses Latin terms
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: praitorion, kenturion, phragelloo in this chapter.

claims.claim: the Greek of verse 8 ends on a conjunction
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: the last word before the bracketed endings is gar.

claims.claim: the account ends on the word 'afraid'
claims.basis: Hosted 16:8.

claims.claim: verses 9-20 were quoted by the second century
claims.basis: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.10.5 quotes Mark 16:19 as from "the conclusion of his Gospel".

claims.claim: a cluster of words Mark uses nowhere else
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: 16 of the 99 distinct words in 16:9-20 occur nowhere else in Mark.

claims.claim: several endings survive: shorter, longer, both, and one with an insertion
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Mark 16" and "Codex Bobiensis".

claims.claim: 1 Corinthians 15 is earlier than the gospels
claims.basis: Wikipedia: the letter is dated AD 53-57. The briefing dates Mark from the mid-60s, with earlier dates defended.

claims.claim: a woman's testimony carried little weight
claims.basis: Josephus, Antiquities 4.8.15: "let not the testimony of women be admitted". Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:8.

claims.claim: the young man: the same word as in 14:51
claims.basis: Tagged Greek: neaniskos only at 14:51 and 16:5.

claims.claim: a few groups handle snakes in worship, with deaths
claims.basis: Wikipedia, "Snake handling in Christianity": "over 100 documented deaths".
